$comment: ★★ A `.s` WHOSE LAST LINE HAS NO NEWLINE ASSEMBLES AND RUNS (P68 round 8, D-ASM-LAST-LINE-WITHOUT-A-NEWLINE-REFUSED). The final byte of `main.s` is the `t` of `ret` — no `\n` follows it. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23: GNU as 2.42 (WSL x86_64 and native mingw-w64) assembles such a file with 'end of file not at end of a line; newline inserted' and the program returns 42; clang 18.1.3 accepts it silently. DSS refused it on every target and configuration with `P_MissingRequiredChild ... got '<eof>'`, because the dialect's grammar requires a `LineEnd` on every line and the end of input supplied none. ★ THE FIX IS A DECLARATION, NOT A SPECIAL CASE: `asm-x86_64-att.lang.json` declares `endOfInputImplies: "\n"`, and the tokenizer reads a text lacking it as if it ended with it. The grammar's line boundary stays mandatory and the user's buffer is never rewritten; the implied `LineEnd` is a zero-width token at the end, like `Eof`. ★ RED-ON-DISABLE: remove `endOfInputImplies` from the dialect and this example is refused again with the same `P_MissingRequiredChild`. ⚠ `.gitattributes` pins `examples/**` to LF, which normalizes line ENDINGS but never adds a final newline, so the missing newline survives every checkout. The `ret` is load-bearing: were the unterminated line lost, `main` would fall off its end. WHAT THE `release` ARM PROVES, NARROWLY: an assembly source forms no HIR/MIR, so no optimizer pass can touch it; the arm pins only that naming the release pipeline does not break the assembly path.
